evals.prompt: I need to migrate my SAP Build Process Automation project to n8n. Here is the archive: evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar
evals.expected_output: One or more .workflow.json files produced for bpi.process artifacts, a credential-stubs.json stub, and a report.json. The response includes an ASCII topology diagram per workflow.
assertions: At least one .workflow.json file is produced
Each workflow JSON has top-level keys: name, nodes, connections, settings
credential-stubs.json is produced and lists destination stubs
report.json is produced
Response contains an ASCII topology diagram section
No bearer tokens or live URLs appear in any workflow JSON

evals.prompt: Convert this SBPA export to n8n. The process uses custom variables: evals/files/simpleCustomVariableUsecase.mtar
evals.expected_output: Workflow JSON with an 'Initialize Custom Data' code node that initialises DataObject fields, plus Set/Get custom data nodes. report.json lists any custom-var-unsupported-type entries for non-string fields.
assertions: A node named 'Initialize Custom Data' exists in the emitted workflow
report.json entries with kind 'custom-var-unsupported-type' appear for object/array fields
Each workflow JSON passes node scripts/validate.js without errors
Response explains which custom variables required workarounds

evals.prompt: How does SBPA to n8n migration work? I don't have an archive yet.
evals.expected_output: Explanation of the migration process pointing at references/SBPA_READING_GUIDE.md and references/activity-mapping.md. The converter script is NOT run and no workflow JSON is produced.
assertions: No node scripts/migrate.js command is executed
No .workflow.json files are produced
Response references the SBPA reading guide or activity mapping reference
Response describes the overall migration approach

evals.prompt: Convert this SAP Build Process Automation project to n8n: evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar. Make sure you write all required lifecycle documents.
evals.expected_output: Three lifecycle documents written: assets/intent.md, assets/product-requirements-document.md, and assets/specification.md. Each file must have real content derived from the archive, not placeholder text. The framing uses the business use case, never the word 'migration'.
assertions: assets/intent.md is written with a title framing the business use case (no 'migration' in the title)
assets/product-requirements-document.md is written after assets/intent.md
assets/specification.md is written after assets/product-requirements-document.md
Each of the three lifecycle files contains real content — no '<placeholder>' tokens remain
assets/intent.md includes a Fit Gap Analysis table
assets/product-requirements-document.md references the Fit Gap Analysis rather than duplicating the gap table
assets/specification.md contains a node-mapping table for at least one bpi.process

evals.prompt: I want to convert my SAP Build Process Automation project to n8n. The archive is at evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar. Run the converter, then show me the topology of every emitted workflow.
evals.expected_output: The converter (node scripts/migrate.js) is run before the lifecycle documents are written. The final response contains an ASCII topology diagram for every emitted workflow under a single '## n8n workflow topology' heading.
assertions: node scripts/migrate.js is run before assets/intent.md is written
The converter output is read as reference only — validate.js is NOT run on the converter output
The response contains a '## n8n workflow topology' heading
At least one ASCII diagram (boxes, arrows) appears under that heading
Each workflow emitted by the skill has a corresponding topology diagram

evals.prompt: Convert this SAP Build Process Automation archive to n8n: evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar. I need the final workflow JSON validated before you're done.
evals.expected_output: The skill generates each .workflow.json from scratch (not by copying the converter output), then runs 'node scripts/validate.js' on every generated file. If validation fails, the JSON is fixed and validate.js is rerun until it passes.
assertions: node scripts/validate.js is called on the generated workflow JSON, not on the converter output
The generated workflow JSON is distinct from the converter output (not a copy)
Every node in the generated workflow has: a unique name, a valid type (package.node format), a numeric typeVersion, a [x,y] position, and an object parameters field
If validate.js fails, the agent fixes the JSON and reruns rather than stopping
The word 'migration' does not appear in any generated workflow node name or connection label

evals.prompt: Convert evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar to n8n. Every node type must come from the node-discovery tools.
evals.expected_output: search_nodes (or list-supported-nodes) is called at least once before the workflow JSON is written. No node type is invented from general n8n knowledge — every type used in the JSON can be traced to a search_nodes / list-supported-nodes lookup result.
assertions: search_nodes or list-supported-nodes is called before the workflow JSON is written
Every node type in the generated workflow JSON uses the package.node format (e.g. n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest, CUSTOM.sapTaskCenter)
No node type appears that was not returned by the node-discovery lookup
The workflow JSON does not contain node types invented from general n8n knowledge (e.g. n8n-nodes-base.sapBapi, n8n-nodes-base.sbpa)

evals.prompt: Convert evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar to n8n and set up the solution structure so it's ready to deploy.
evals.expected_output: After the workflow JSON is validated, the setup-solution skill is invoked to place asset.yaml and solution.yaml. Both files are present in the solution directory when the skill finishes.
assertions: The setup-solution skill is invoked after the workflow JSON passes validation
asset.yaml is present in the solution directory
solution.yaml is present in the solution directory
The skill does not stop after writing the workflow JSON — it proceeds through setup-solution

evals.prompt: Convert evals/files/simpleCustomVariableUsecase.mtar to n8n. Tell me upfront about any gaps or unsupported constructs before you start writing files.
evals.expected_output: After running the converter, the skill surfaces every report.json item and every known under-development construct (RuleTask → CUSTOM.sapAgent, non-string custom variables, boundary timers) before writing assets/intent.md. The Fit Gap Analysis in intent.md captures these gaps.
assertions: The converter is run and report.json is read before any lifecycle document is written
Known constraints (custom-var-unsupported-type, RuleTask under-development) are surfaced to the user before assets/intent.md is written
The Fit Gap Analysis table in assets/intent.md lists the gaps identified from report.json
assets/product-requirements-document.md references the Fit Gap Analysis rather than restating every gap
The agent does not silently work around unsupported constructs

evals.prompt: Can you convert this SBPA archive to n8n: evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar? Keep the original activity names as node names in the workflow.
evals.expected_output: Node names in the generated workflow JSON match the human-readable labels from the SBPA process's translations.units block, not machine IDs. The workflow is recognisable after import into n8n.
assertions: Node names in the generated workflow JSON come from the SBPA process translations (human-readable labels), not from internal SBPA IDs
No node is named with a UUID or machine-generated identifier
Node names in the topology diagram match the node names in the workflow JSON

evals.prompt: Convert evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar to n8n. The process uses an ExclusiveGateway — make sure the decision logic is translated correctly.
evals.expected_output: ExclusiveGateway maps to n8n-nodes-base.if. Conditions use n8n expression syntax translated from the SBPA JUEL conditions (${...} expressions). No SBPA formula-language constructs (Map(), path.dot.notation) are used inside IF node conditions.
assertions: ExclusiveGateway nodes in the SBPA process map to n8n-nodes-base.if nodes in the output
IF node conditions use n8n expression syntax, not raw JUEL or SBPA formula syntax
JUEL word-form operators (eq, gt, and, not, mod, empty) are translated to their n8n equivalents
The decision gate (JUEL vs mapping formula) from references/formula-grammar.md is applied: ${...} conditions go through the JUEL path, not the formula path
No untranslated ${...} or #{...} tokens remain in the generated workflow JSON

evals.prompt: I have an SBPA project but I just want to understand what processes it contains before committing to a full conversion. Archive: evals/files/SimpleOrderManagement.mtar
evals.expected_output: The skill unpacks the archive, builds the process inventory and dependency graph (per references/intent-extraction.md), and reports: process names, identifiers, trigger types, sub-workflow dependencies, and destination names. The converter is run (it is needed for inventory), but no lifecycle documents are written and the user is not committed to a full conversion.
assertions: The archive is unpacked and the process inventory is built
The response lists every bpi.process found: name, identifier, trigger type
Sub-workflow dependencies (ReferencedSubflow targets) are identified and listed
Destination names from environment-variable artifacts are listed
The user is informed of any gaps or unsupported constructs found during inventory
